title: Your Agent Reads Your Documents
subtitle: Monday your agent answers questions about this course from its own documents — syllabus, briefs, schedule — and cites the passage. Wednesday it reads the document that matters to you, goes into your midterm agent, and you get thirty minutes of midterm time.
heroTitle: Your Agent Reads Your Documents

objectives.title: Ground It · Cite It · Catch It Lying
objectives.description: The one outcome: an agent that answers only from your documents, cites the passage for every fact, says 'not found' instead of guessing, and treats documents as data rather than instructions.

objectives.title: See the Three Levels
objectives.description: The model alone invents a policy. Pasting everything in is correct and expensive. A thirty-line search tool retrieves three passages, cites them, and costs a fraction. Same loop as Session 6.

objectives.title: Break It Four Ways
objectives.description: A cross-document question, a question the documents never answer, an outdated syllabus in the same folder, and a document that gives the agent orders. Then fix one in one place.

objectives.title: Put It in Your Agent
objectives.description: Your own document on Wednesday, ten lines into your midterm notebook, and the business questions: does it cite, what happens when the document is old, who can edit what it reads.

agenda.title: Part 5 Together: When Does It Fail?
agenda.description: Cross-document, not-in-the-documents, the outdated Spring syllabus, and the campus FAQ that gives the agent orders. Fix one in one place.
bulletPoints: Did it say 'not in the documents' or invent a number?
Did it notice OUTDATED, or average two semesters?
Did it obey a sentence inside a document? That is prompt injection through documents — the attack Argon advertises resistance to

activities.discussionNote: Every 'chat with your documents' product is this notebook with a login page. Buying one is fine. Being sold one without the four questions is not.

takeaways.text: Ground it. A tool that returns passages with their source, and a prompt that answers only from them. The model's memory is not a document.
The citation is the audit. Level 0 had none, Level 1 buried it, Level 2 points at it. Air Canada paid for not having one.
Documents are data, not instructions. A sentence inside a file can try to give your agent orders. Who can edit what it reads is the new attack surface.
Every shared drive has a Spring syllabus in it. 'Not found' and 'outdated' are answers. Averaging two semesters is not.
Retrieval is the cheap part. Thirty lines, no key. What you pay for is the reading, and retrieval makes the reading small.
